This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
2. Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell:

It is the case of petitioner that, on 07.09.2021 at about 7.55 a.m., when the petitioner was proceeding as an inmate in PIAGGIO APE-Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-42-3740 from her home to M/s LEL International Pvt. Ltd.,, Chandana Hosahalli, Dabaspet, Nelamangala Taluk where the petitioner is working as a Tailor and when the said auto reached at Hosapalya cross, Mudalpalya-Shivgange road,
Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, at that time, the driver of the said auto drove the said Auto in rash and negligent manner and turtled down and thereby the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

It is further urged that soon after the accident she was shifted to J.P. Hospital, Nelamangala wherein she took first aid treatment and thereafter she was admitted to ESI Hospital, Rajajinagar, further she was shifted to M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru wherein she underwent surgery and discharged with an advise of bed rest for 6 months and follow-up treatment and till date she is under follow-up treatment.

She has spent Rs.50,000/-
towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and attendant charges etc.

It is further urged that the petitioner was hale and healthy and doing Tailoring work in M/s LEL International Pvt. Ltd.
and also she was doing bulk tailoring work at her home and earning monthly income of Rs.25,000/-.

It is further urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent act of the driver of the Ape auto as such the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation and prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. After service of notice respondent No.1 spurred in rush to the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that, the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts and liable to be dismissed.

The respondent No.1 admitted that he is the RC owner cum driver of the Ape Passenger Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-42-3740 and was duly insured with the 2nd respondent and same was in force as on the date of accident.
It is further submitted that the driver of auto also possess valid and effective driving licence.

The respondent No.1 contended that on 07.09.2021 he was driving the Auto with two passengers on Mudalapalya to Shivagange road,
Nelamanagala at about 7.30 a.m, one Dog abruptly came across the road and to avoid the dog he applied sudden break, consequently said auto fell down on its left side.
Further he submitted that after three days of the accident the petitioner colluded with the jurisdictional police have filed a false complaint against this respondent.
The police have filed chargesheet against the driver and owner of the Ape auto.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.

Hence prayed to dismiss the Vajramma G vs Somashekhar on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70412007/
2 petition.

4. After service of notice, respondent No.2 spurred in rush to the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
It has admitted that this respondent is the insurer of Auto rickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA- 42-3740 and liability to indemnify is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.

Non -compliance of section's 134(c) and 158(6)
of MV Act is pleaded.
Further it is averred that there is a delay in lodging the complaint and no valid reasons assigned for the delay in lodging the complaint.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the Autorickshaw did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
Further it is urged that as on the date of accident the insured Autorickshaw did not holding valid and effective Permit and FC and further carrying excess seating capacity as on the date of accident.
Hence the jurisdictional police after thorough investigation have filed charge sheet under Sec.177, 181, 192(A) 187 of MV Act.
Further it is submitted that the said auto rickshaw was not having valid permit to ply in place of accident and carrying excess seating capacity as on the date of accident.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor-in-office framed the following :
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she met with a Road Traffic Accident on 07.09.2021 at about 7.55 a.m, near Hosapalya Cross, Mudalapalya - Shivagange road, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of PIAGGIO Ape Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-42- 3740 ?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that she is entitled to the compensation amount claimed ?

If so from whom and to what extent ?
3. What order or award ?
6. In support of the case of the petitioner, the petitioner stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P15 documents.

Furthermore the respondent No.2 has also examined its Executive Legal officer as RW.2 and got marked Ex.R.4 & 5 documents.
The Respondent No.1 owner cum driver of Auto got himself examined as RW.3 and got marked Ex.R.6 and 7 documents.

Before dwelling into analyzing the disputed facts in issue it is relevant to have the birds eye of the case of petitioner in a nutshell.

On the other hand respondent No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurance company have attacked the case of the petitioner on various prisms known to fact and law.

It is the specific contention of the respondent no.1 being the owner that he was the one he was driving the autorickshaw at the time of accident and the said autorickshaw is covered by the insurance of respondent No.2, as such the respondent No.2 is liable to indemnify respondent No.1.

13. Per contra, the respondent No.2 contended that the driver of the Autorickshaw did not possess valid & effective DL and the said auto rickshaw was not having valid permit to ply in place of accident and carrying excess seating capacity as on the date of accident.

14. In support of these contentions, the respondent No.2 has examined the Investigating Officer as RW.1 and Ex.R.1 to 3 were got marked.

15. On dissection of materials placed on record, after marshaling of facts in issue and after hearing erudite counsel appearing for combating parties, this Tribunal opines that this issue is pregmented with inner issues such as :
1) Whether delay of 3 days in filing the FIS is fatal to the case of the petitioner ?
2) Whether respondent No.1 proves that who was driving the Autorichshaw on the date of accident ?
3) Whether the respondent No.2 demonstrates that the driver of the Autorichshaw was driving the vehicle with six inmates and that adds to the negligence ?
4) Whether the petitioner has demonstrated the factum of negligence on the part of insured vehicle ?
16.
Now let me unfurl each of the contention urged by the rival parties in the light of oral and documentary proof.
It is the specific contention of the petitioner that, she has sustained grievous injuries in the RTA on 07.09.2021.
The Criminal law was set into motion on 10.09.2021 at about 4.00 p.m, which is reflected in Ex.P.2 FIS.
It could be borne out from the FIS itself that injured was taken to different hospitals for treatment as such there was a delay in lodging FIS for 3 days.
It could be borne out from the medical records itself discloses that injured very severely injured in RTA.
Further Ex.P.14 being the MLC memo dated 07.09.2021 itself cures the defect of delay in setting criminal law into motion.
Added more, when the petitioner is fighting for her life, the relatives of the petitioner cannot be expected to set criminal law in motion.
The predominant responsibility of the family of the injured will be saving the kith and kin's life rather fighting for justice.

There is a delay of 3 days and that delay is well explained by the petitioner in this regard it is relevant to relied on the Vajramma G vs Somashekhar on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70412007/
5 decision reported in Ravi v. Badrinarayan and others reported in AIR 2011 SC 1226, wherein the Hon'ble Aoex Court has observed as hereunder :

sentences.text: "The purpose of lodging the FIR in motor accident cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquillity of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if there is delay, the same deserve to be condoned.
In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground."
(Emphasis supplied by me).
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The ratio decidendi laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court is aptly applicable to the facts of the instant case.
The petitioner had explained the delay caused.
The petitioner clearly demonstrated as to the involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident.
17. The next seminal question to be considered is with regard to the driver of the offending Auto vehicle.
It is the specific defence of respondent No.1 who is the RC owner of the offending vehicle that, he was the one who is driving the Autorickshaw at the time of accident and not his son by name Deepak.

On the other hand, it is the crux of the defense of respondent No.2 that it is one Deepak who is son of respondent No.1 by himself driving the autorickshaw and jurisdictional police after thorough investigation have filed chargesheet as against one Deepak who is son of respondent No.1.
When this being rival contentions urged by the combating parties it is relevant to fall back upon the oral and documentary proof to that effect.

In order to show that, respondent No.1 was driving the autorickshaw there are absolutely no materials placed on record except the self-serving and self-proclaimed statement of respondent No.1 who is examined as RW.3.
He during his chief- examination has deposed that he himself was driving the auto and only two passengers were there in the autorickshaw on the day of accident.

When he was subjected to litmus test of cross- examination Vajramma G vs Somashekhar on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70412007/
6 he categorically admitted pertaining to ownership over the autorickshaw and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Added more Ex.P.2
being the complaint is also lodged against the son of respondent No.1
. RW.3 categorically admitted as to the lodging of FIR.
It is specific contention of respondent No.1 that, he himself was driving the autorickahw.
The evidence of RW.3 discloses that he has not challenged the chargesheet.
Further more it is a trite law that the tribunal has to assess the materials placed on record independently without getting influenced by the chargesheet.
When this prelude in the backdrop if this court navigates through the evidence of PW.1 who is injured and she is also the eye witness to the accident.
She categorically admitted that, it is the respondent No.1 who was the driver of autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-42-3740.
The said categorical admission of PW.1 reads as here under : It is true to suggest that on the day of accident the respondent No.1 was driving the Ape auto bearing Reg.No.KA-42-3740.
This categorical admission coupled with unimpeached evidence of RW.3 reveals that, respondent No.1 himself was driving the autorickahw on the ill-fated day of accident.

This admission of PW.1 cannot be considered as a stray admission in the eye of law for a simple reason that PW.1 is also the eye-witness to the accident and she can well deposed about who was driving the autorickshaw as on the date of accident.
The said categorical admission of PW.1 cannot be brushed aside.
The respondent No.1 had clearly demonstrated with the help of oral evidence that he was driving the autorickshaw.
18. The next aspect to be considered with regard to the factum of negligence.
The negligence has to be proved in MACT cases as the any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty:
For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.
Damages:
At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of Vajramma G vs Somashekhar on 12 June, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70412007/
7 recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
19. Reverting back to the factual matrix, the document which sheds light on the factum of rash and negligence is Ex.P.5 being the Spot Mahazar.
This court gave anxious consideration on astuteness to the contents of the above said document.
On conspectus reading of Ex.P.5 it reflects that the accident happened on the Nelamangala to Shivagange road, near Hosapalya gate.
On close perusal of the same it reflects that, the accident happend beause of the rashness and negligence of Autorickshaw driver.
Further the contents of the Ex.P.5 is fortified by the Ex.P.7 IMV Report and IMV inspector opined that the accident occured was not due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.
20. Above all even the chargesheet was also filed as against the driver of Autorickshaw the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 and 338 of IPC and 177, 181, 192(A), 187 of IMV Act.
This court is aware of the fact that chargesheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.5 which was read in consonance with the Ex.P.3 Chargesheet.
There is no qualm in the preposition of law that an chargesheet is not a sole document on which the factum of negligence has to be decided.

In the instant case on hand, having regard to the other circumstances and other documentary proof it is crystal clear that there was absolutely negligence on the part of the driver of the Autorickshaw in which the petitioner was proceeding as passenger.
21. No doubt the respondent No.2 has examined the Investigating Officer as RW.1 has produced Ex.R.1 to 3 being the chargesheet, 133 Notice and Reply given by the owner of the insured Autorickshaw.
On careful perusal of Ex.R.3 wherein the owner of the offending Autorickshaw has admitted the involvement of the vehicle.
It is also forthcoming from Ex.R3 reply to 133 notice that the driver of the vehicle was not having valid DL at the time of accident.
Be that as it may, the liability will be discussed in the later part of this judgment.
Therefore it is crystal clear that the offending vehicle is caused accident and in the accident the petitioner sustained injury.
Further Ex.P.5 being the Spot mahazar spells out there is a negligence on the part of the driver of the offending autorickshaw.

Further the police records and oral and documentary evidence of the petitioner are proved that the accident was occurred on the sole negligence of driver of offending Autorikshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-42-3741.
In the accident the petitioner has sustained injury.
22. The another lap of arguments canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 is that carrying of exces passenger in the autorickshaw has also contributed for negligence.

In order to controvert the above said contention, it is urged that Simply because there is a violation of any law,
there is no presumption that there is contributory negligence on the part of the person.
It is to be decided in the facts and circumstances of each case.
That is to say, some other additional evidence is necessary to attribute contributory negligence to the driver of the autorickshaw who was carrying 6 passengers in the autorickshaw.
No independent evidence is given by respondent No.2 in this regard.
To put it differently, if a person drives a vehicle with excess passengers, he commits an offence.

The same by itself may not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident.

8 23.
Though PW.1 was cross-examined at length by respondent No.2 counsel but nothing fatal was elicited so as to distrust the petitioner's version in his chief-examination.
Even the chargesheet as per Ex.P.3 is also filed as against the driver of the Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-42-3740.
When such the case absolutely there is no impediment in considering the version of the petitioner herein.
The petitioner has successfully demonstrated there is a negligence on the part of the driver of autorickshaw.
Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Autorickshaw.
On assessing entire evidence the light of oral and documentary proof, the preponderance of probability tilts infavour of petitioner herein.

Hence, this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 'In the Affirmative'.
24. ISSUE NO.2 :

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : (i)
Right clavicle fracture (ii) Swelling + tenderness over right shoulder present.

The discharge summary issued by M.S.
Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru
indicate that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for the period from 07.09.2021 to 11.09.2021 (5 days in total).
During the course of treatment she had undergone surgery in the form of : ORIF + Plating (6 hole plating).
Therefore she is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
25. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY & LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD :
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries she has become disabled and lost her earning capacity.

Therefore she got examined Dr.S.A. Somashekara as PW.2, who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has total permanent physical disability of the right upper limb at 27% and whole body disability at 13%.
It is elicited during the course of cross-examination that PW.2 is that the petitioner sustained only right clavicle fracture and the said fracture is united with implants in situ.
It is also admitted that if the difficulties are there it will be mentioned in the follow up records.
Further he admitted that the petitioner was advised only to take the medication prescribed.
When the say of doctor there are no complications at the fracture side then there is no question of disability to the tune of 13%.
26. It is relevant to note that, Clavicle bone means (collarbone) is a long, slightly curved bone that connects your arm to your body.
The said bone can be found one on both sides of the base of the neck.
The bones help keep a shoulder blade in the correct position as a person move.
The word "clavicle" comes from the Latin "clavicula," which translates to "little key."
The bone is actually shaped a bit like an old-fashioned key.
And it works in much the same way.
When one rotate a key, it moves the lock.
Similarly, when a person lift a arm, a clavicle rotates along its axis to allow movement.
The clavicle, or collarbone, is a slender, S-shaped long bone approximately 6 inches (15 cm) long that serves as a strut between the shoulder blade and the sternum (breastbone).
There are two clavicles, one on the left and one on the right.

The clavicle is the only long bone in the body that lies Vajramma G vs Somashekhar on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70412007/
9 horizontally.
Together with the shoulder blade, it makes up the shoulder girdle.
It is a palpable bone and, in people who have less fat in this region, the location of the bone is clearly visible.
It receives its name from Latin clavicula 'little key' because the bone rotates along its axis like a key when the shoulder is abducted.
The clavicle is the most commonly fractured bone.
It can easily be fractured by impacts to the shoulder from the force of falling on outstretched arms or by a direct hit.
27. It is relevant to note that, Clavicle or collar bone is a slender S shaped bone approximately 6 inches that serves as a strut between the shoulder blade and the sternum.
Together with the shoulder blade, it makes up the shoulder griddle.
To put it differently, clavicle bone is not a separate component of the arm but just a supporting bone.
It is in this view of the matter, no disability is prescribed for clavicle fracture in the Government of India guidelines 2018.
Despite of it, PW.2 has assessed the whole body disability of the petitioner at 13% which is totally contrary to the guidelines.
Be that as it may as the clavicle fracture does not lead to any disability the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
28. Further it is to be seen whether the aforesaid disability impairs the avocation of the petitioner.

As per the averments made in her evidence affidavit, at the time of accident the petitioner was doing Tailoring work in M/s LEL International Pvt. Ltd. and also she was doing bulk tailoring work at her home and earning monthly income of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
To substantiate the same she has not produced any iota of documents nor employer of the petitioner is not examined before this Tribunal.
29. This court also does not loose sight on the fact that even PW.1 herself had categorically admitted with regard to her future income as here under : "I am an ESI card holder.
It was issued by my employer where I was working (M/s. LEL International Pvt. Ltd.,).
I was paid a salary of Rs.12,000/- p.m.
Salary was directly credited to my bank account.
I have a bank account at Canara bank.
I can produce my bank bass book."
It could be ascertained from the materials placed on record and the admission of PWl herself that at the time of accident she was paid a salary of Rs.12,000/-".
Further she stated that at present she was not working anywhere.
Further she had also not produced bank account statement to show that she was not earning any income during laid up period but for the best reasons known to her she failed to produce the same.

In this regard reliance is placed upon the decision reported in AIR 1964 SC 136 wherein it is held that '(e) Evidence Act (1872), S.114 - All relevant documents admitted to have been in existence not placed before Court by party concerned - Adverse inference has to be drawn against party.'
30.
The discussion supra goes to show petitioner has neither been terminated from her job on account of accidental injuries nor she has suffered any financial loss during the laid-up period.

Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
31.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

per day and a sum of Rs.10,000/- (2,000 X 5) is awarded under this head.
32. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
33. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As per the bills marked at Ex.P9, the petitioner has spent Rs.5,712/-
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of her cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.5,712/- which is rounded off to Rs.5,800/- towards medical expenses.
34. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:

On examination of the petitioner the doctor witness has noted the following : the petitioner has a wasting of right shoulder girdle and right upper limb is seen, surgical scars are seen over right shoulder and clavicle.
The recent x-ray of the united fracture right clavicle with AC joint disruption with implants in situ.

Under such circumstances certainly there would be some sort of discomfort which would come in the way of effective discharge of the duties of the petitioner and for that she needs to be compensated suitably.
Having regard to this aspect, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
35. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants for which he may require Rs.30,000/-.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.

During the course of cross examination PW.2 categorically admitted that "it is true to suggest that if the petitioner is having ESI facility, she would get her implants removal surgery done free of cost at ESI Hospital.
Further on close perusal of cross examination of PW.1 she categorically admitted that "I am an ESI Card holder.
It was issued by my employer where I was working".
But undisputedly petitioner has to undergo surgery for removal of implants, for which she has to necessarily bear certain expenses.

Thus she is entitled to Rs.10,000/-
towards future medical and other incidental expenses.

sentences.text: Further much was canvassed by leaned counsel for respondent No.2 that the chargesheet is filed against the driver of the Autorickshaw for the offence punishable u/s 181 and 187 of IPC but under issue No.1 it is crystal clear that the accident happened when the respondent No.1 himself was driving the autorickshaw.
Much was canvassed by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 by relying of 133 Notice and reply to the 133 notice.
As already held above, it is the specific contention of the respondent No.1 that, jurisdictional police have taken the signatures to the blank paper and as such got created Ex.R.2 and 3 documents.
This court gave anxious consideration to the contents of Ex.R.2 and 3.
On careful perusal of Ex.R.2 being the 133 Notice itself this court can find the signatures of respondent No.1 at the end of the page.
It is the notice issued to the respondent No.1.
Added more in Ex.R.3 being the reply notice, again the signature of respondent No.1 is found at the extreme lower right side of the page.
The evidence of PW.1 coupled with evidence of RW.3 and is doubtful circumstances found in Ex.R.2 and 3 categorically reflects that the driver of the vehicle was implanted.
Hence beyond any stretch of imagination it cannot be conceded that one Deepak was driving the Autorickshaw at the time of accident.

Further in the evidence of respondent No.1,
respondent No.1 has produced his DL which is marked as Ex.R.7.
The discussions made under issue No.1 reveals that it is respondent No.1 who was driving the autorickshaw.
The IO who is examined as RW.1 has invoked sec.3(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act on the basis that one Deepak was not having valid DL at the time of accident.
The respondent No.1 had demonstrated that he was driving the Autorickshaw.
Ex . R.7
discloses that respondent No.1 is having valid DL.
When such being the case the respondent No.1 has not violated any terms of the policy.
39. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-42-3740 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that she met with a Road Traffic Accident on 07.09.2021 at about 7.55 a.m, near Hosapalya Cross, Mudalapalya - Shivagange road, Kasaba Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, Bengaluru District and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent driving of PIAGGIO Ape Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-42- 3740 ?
2. Whether the petitioner proves that she is entitled to the compensation amount claimed ?
If so from whom and to what extent ?
3. What order or award ?
15. On dissection of materials placed on record, after marshaling of facts in issue and after hearing erudite counsel appearing for combating parties, this Tribunal opines that this issue is pregmented with inner issues such as :
1) Whether delay of 3 days in filing the FIS is fatal to the case of the petitioner ?
2) Whether respondent No.1 proves that who was driving the Autorichshaw on the date of accident ?
3) Whether the respondent No.2 demonstrates that the driver of the Autorichshaw was driving the vehicle with six inmates and that adds to the negligence ?
4) Whether the petitioner has demonstrated the factum of negligence on the part of insured vehicle ?
16.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Added more, when the petitioner is fighting for her life, the relatives of the petitioner cannot be expected to set criminal law in motion.
The predominant responsibility of the family of the injured will be saving the kith and kin's life rather fighting for justice.
If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground."
(Emphasis supplied by me).
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.
If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The petitioner had explained the delay caused.
The petitioner clearly demonstrated as to the involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident.
It is the specific defence of respondent No.1 who is the RC owner of the offending vehicle that, he was the one who is driving the Autorickshaw at the time of accident and not his son by name Deepak.
In order to show that, respondent No.1 was driving the autorickshaw there are absolutely no materials placed on record except the self-serving and self-proclaimed statement of respondent No.1 who is examined as RW.3.
This categorical admission coupled with unimpeached evidence of RW.3 reveals that, respondent No.1 himself was driving the autorickahw on the ill-fated day of accident.
This admission of PW.1 cannot be considered as a stray admission in the eye of law for a simple reason that PW.1 is also the eye-witness to the accident and she can well deposed about who was driving the autorickshaw as on the date of accident.
The said categorical admission of PW.1 cannot be brushed aside.
The respondent No.1 had clearly demonstrated with the help of oral evidence that he was driving the autorickshaw.
The negligence has to be proved in MACT cases as the any other fact in issue.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Breach of Duty:
After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
This court is aware of the fact that chargesheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.5 which was read in consonance with the Ex.P.3 Chargesheet.
There is no qualm in the preposition of law that an chargesheet is not a sole document on which the factum of negligence has to be decided.
In the instant case on hand, having regard to the other circumstances and other documentary proof it is crystal clear that there was absolutely negligence on the part of the driver of the Autorickshaw in which the petitioner was proceeding as passenger.
To put it differently, if a person drives a vehicle with excess passengers, he commits an offence.
Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Autorickshaw.
It receives its name from Latin clavicula 'little key' because the bone rotates along its axis like a key when the shoulder is abducted.
The clavicle is the most commonly fractured bone.
It can easily be fractured by impacts to the shoulder from the force of falling on outstretched arms or by a direct hit.
Together with the shoulder blade, it makes up the shoulder griddle.
To put it differently, clavicle bone is not a separate component of the arm but just a supporting bone.
It is in this view of the matter, no disability is prescribed for clavicle fracture in the Government of India guidelines 2018.
Despite of it, PW.2 has assessed the whole body disability of the petitioner at 13% which is totally contrary to the guidelines.
Be that as it may as the clavicle fracture does not lead to any disability the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
The respondent No.1 had demonstrated that he was driving the Autorickshaw.
When such being the case the respondent No.1 has not violated any terms of the policy.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-42-3740 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
